# Storyboard — The ferment log

Status: full planning proposal, not approved or built. Design choices delegated by Ines; final review pending. Working titles below describe content, not final captions or opening copy.

## Waiting on Ines before publication
1. Public email and workshop/application routes; whether applications are open and whether an existing site is being replaced. Until then, plan enquiries rather than invented vacancies, schedules or transactions.
2. Owned pot and larder image files. Text faces are the complete fallback; no stock imagery impersonates her work.
3. Restaurant permission before Priya's images appear, with Priya Nair credit; Olu's permission before scans containing his drawings appear. Staff faces remain excluded without confirmed consent. These assets are optional, not prerequisites for the concept.
4. Any remaining unconfirmed metrics or project details only if Ines wants them added. They are omitted from this script.

## Idea
Question: **What happens before the menu is written?**

One continuous scroll follows six paper leaves from a ferment log. Their arrangements expose the evidence: influences, dates, log fields, work, measurements and the invitation to learn more. The menu comes last because Ines says it does. The conceptual answer is preparation, recording and checking before the weekly menu; final wording remains to be written and reviewed.

The log is a website interpretation, not a reproduction of an unseen notebook. No invented dates, salt ratios, recipes, handwriting, handwritten ticks or batch outcomes. No implication that a reader has learned safe fermentation from a visual diagram.

## Chapters
| Chapter | Name in form | Role | Content | Same six leaves | Interaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Started | Opening/origins | Identity, central question, influences | Shallow stack opens to pot/influence faces | Skip to enquiries; jump navigation |
| 2 | Date | Who/where | Career dates, with honest stage description | Spread into an ordered date line | Accessible date-detail disclosures |
| 3 | Salt | How | Prep list and actual log fields | Align into one readable working spread | Select field explanations, all also in text |
| 4 | Checks | What | Larder, labels, koji cupboard; teaching and Brine | Turn into a two-by-three evidence grid | Open owned image details; jump to workshop enquiry |
| 5 | Ready | Outcomes/testimony | Kitchen waste result and Callum's words; menu written last | Two leaves compare figures, one exposes quote | Read measurement context and quote |
| 6 | Next batch | Answer/contact | Invite apprentice, writer and workshop enquiries | Reassemble into the original stack with last leaf visible | Three labelled contact routes |

## Beats
Desktop screens are approximate viewport heights of ordinary scroll, not forced slides. Total about 8.5 screens; natural content height takes priority. No scroll interception or compulsory waiting.

| Beat | Screens | Arrangement | Faces | Additions | Caption working title and source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1a | 1 | All six as shallow open stack; pot leaf visible | Owned pot photograph if supplied; influence names on another leaf | HTML identity, question, proof and enquiry shortcut | Origins; F1, F16, F20, U1f |
| 1b | 0.5 | Top leaves gently separate | Sandor Katz/book names and own pot detail; no book-cover reproduction | None | Influences named; F16, no invented lesson |
| 2a | 1 | Six leaves spread along a horizontal date line | Education 2014–16; Brassica 2016–19; stage inset Jan–Mar 2018; Corn Exchange 2019–22; acting March 2022; Head Chef September 2022 | HTML dates give precise month ranges; no travel map | Experience; F9–F12, U1a, U1c |
| 2b | 0.5 | Stage leaf comes forward; others retain chronology | Ten-week unpaid stage; jar washing/labelling; helped with two garum batches | None | Stage responsibilities; U1a. No researcher claim or invented career turning point |
| 3a | 1 | Four leaves align as field columns; two form supporting stack | Date started / salt / check days / ready; names only, no fabricated entries | HTML explains fields and prep-list role | Working record; U1j |
| 3b | 0.5 | Same spread exposes a last leaf after the log fields | Menu written last, represented by sourced words; no invented menu | None | Order of work; U1j |
| 4a | 1 | Two-by-three evidence grid | Own larder photo, own label crop if cleared; remaining faces use sourced text on cupboard, staff meal, workshops and Brine | HTML work index also lists apprentice programme and Sunday Pot, using only sourced descriptions | Work at a glance; F2–F3, F13–F15, F19; unresolved credits/figures omitted |
| 4b | 0.5 | One evidence leaf enlarges; others remain in grid | Owned larder/label detail, when supplied | Keyboard-accessible image detail; never reveal prices or unconsented faces | Inspect the record; F19, U1i–U1j |
| 5a | 1 | Two leaves sit side by side, a third stays behind | 14 kg/week and 5 kg/week with measurement context | HTML explicitly says “we”, whole-kitchen prep and plate waste, weighed over one month in 2023; bones excluded because they go to stock | Kitchen result; U1b. No annual extrapolation, sole credit or causal claim about a particular ferment |
| 5b | 0.5 | Quote leaf turns forward; figures remain present | Exact supplied Callum quote and attribution | Menu-last connection remains process, not proof that one caused the other | Owner testimony; F17, U1g; U1j |
| 6a | 1 | All six reunite; final leaf faces reader | Working invitation titles for apprentices, writers and workshop participants | Full contact section, credits and footer | What happens next; U1h, U1j. No invented availability |

## Thirty-second visit
First viewport: Ines Okafor; Head Chef at Saltmarsh, Leeds; fermentation and apprentice programme; central question; compact proof showing the 14-to-5 kg weekly result with team credit and the full short measurement qualification. Keep proof in HTML, not tiny 3D texture. Enquiry shortcut is immediately visible.

A slim chapter rail exposes Started, Date, Salt, Checks, Ready and Next batch with descriptive accessible labels. Mobile uses a compact jump menu. Anchor URLs work directly; the close has a permanent link. Reader can skip every animation.

## Motion and access
Desktop uses one sticky scene beside ordinary HTML. Scroll gently rotates, spreads and gathers the same leaves. Settled states face the reader; no ongoing spinning, camera flight, custom cursor, parallax text or autoplay sound. Text remains readable during motion. The scene makes ordering, inspection and comparison visible; it does not gate content.

| Where | Experience |
|---|---|
| Phone | Single column; compact static/briefly transitioning paper assembly above chapter text; no full-screen sticky trap. Chronology becomes vertical, evidence grid becomes stacked cards, figures remain a readable pair. No hover interactions; controls at least 44 px. Small phones default to static evidence figures. |
| Reduced motion | No scroll-linked transforms or animated transitions. Static arrangement for each chapter preserves chronology, field order, gallery and comparison. |
| No WebGL | Responsive still images/HTML paper panels at the same chapter positions; all evidence, links and contacts remain. |
| No JavaScript | Server-rendered document with headings, images, native disclosure controls, anchor links and contact links. No loading overlay. |

Semantic headings, skip link, visible focus, sufficient contrast, image descriptions and zoom/reflow support. Duplicate canvas text is hidden from assistive technology; the HTML contains the full information. Image detail dialog, if built, manages focus and Escape correctly. Do not rely on colour or movement for meaning.

## Colour, material and type
Default selected by assistant: **Log paper** — warm paper #F2EBDD, ink #252A24, dark olive accent #46563D. Leaves are matte off-white with faint rules, restrained grain and soft edge shadows; no manufactured stains or false handwriting. Light and texture support legibility.

Alternative studies for a future build, not extra concepts: **Larder label** — ground #E8E8DE, ink #202923, accent #345D55, smooth pale label stock; **Clay and paper** — ground #F3E8DC, ink #352B27, accent #8B4636, thicker cream leaves. Pot colours are unverified; the clay palette is a design option, not sampled from an unseen photograph. Default is Log paper; alternatives can later be compared in scroll, without adding a public theme picker.

Two self-hosted open-source typefaces: **Source Sans 3** for headings, prose and controls; **IBM Plex Mono** for dates, field labels and measured values on the leaves. Comfortable 18–20 px body copy, roughly 60-character lines; large quiet headings rather than screen-filling slogans. Font licences and contrast to be checked during implementation. Meaningful faces have matching readable HTML; no requirement to zoom into a 3D label.

## Everything else
Build means included in a future implementation, not authorization to build now.

| Feature | Decision | Who / reason |
|---|---|---|
| Navigation | Build | Assistant: chapter anchors, skip link and contact shortcut |
| Separate project pages | Later | Assistant: add when documented cases and cleared assets justify them |
| All work listed | Build | Assistant: concise Checks index: larder, apprentice programme, workshops, Brine, Sunday Pot; career stays under Date |
| Contact | Build | Assistant: three purpose-labelled email/booking routes; destinations pending; do not invent addresses |
| CV download | Never in this scope | Assistant, grounded in U1h: not seeking employment; career context already present |
| Testimonial | Build | Ines cleared Callum; use exact quote and owner attribution |
| Languages | Build English; others later | Assistant: supplied language and Leeds audience; no inferred multilingual fluency |
| Shared links and icon | Build | Assistant: accurate title/description, owned or typographic preview, folded log-leaf icon; image rights respected |
| Missing-address page | Build | Assistant: simple route back to story and enquiries |
| Blog | Later | Assistant: Brine listing suffices initially; no invented publication schedule |
| Chat | Never in this scope | Assistant: email and booking routes serve stated audiences |
| Legal notice / privacy | Build as applicable | Assistant: identify actual site operator and data collection before drafting; no assumed blanket UK imprint requirement |
| Booking and payment system | Later | Assistant: link to existing service if supplied; no new checkout without dates/prices/terms |
| Credits | Build | Assistant: unobtrusive asset credits, including Priya when approved |
| Analytics / cookies | Later / omit initially | Assistant: no tracking needed for the proposed experience; reassess with a concrete need |
| Search/social metadata | Build | Assistant: factual person/title/location metadata, canonical URL when known; no fabricated reviews or openings |

## Performance and acceptance for a future build
HTML first; scene loads after readable content. One shared geometry/material set, compressed responsive textures, no physics or continuous idle rendering. Mobile device-pixel-ratio cap; free resources when scene is inactive. Avoid expensive layered transparency. Initial mobile content target under 500 KB compressed excluding deferred 3D; desktop scene budget approximately 1.5 MB. If assets exceed budgets, simplify rather than delay the page.

Check keyboard-only use, reduced motion, JavaScript off, WebGL failure, 320 px width and real touch interaction. Target LCP under 2.5 s, CLS below 0.1, INP under 200 ms on a representative mobile connection; these are implementation targets, not measured results. Verify exact dates, measurement context, quote attribution and asset permissions before launch. Ensure obscured/cropped private content is absent from delivered files, not merely hidden with CSS.

## Decisions and review
Assistant chose the ferment-log concept, six chapters, log-paper palette, two typefaces, modest motion, mobile static default, enquiry-first contact, English, no CV/chat/tracking and deferred project pages. These can be changed without altering the confirmed facts. Full decision record: decided-for-you.md.

Next decision: approve this storyboard or identify changes. Final captions and opening copy are not written at this planning stage. No site implementation has been created; building is outside this skill version.
# Planning handover

Request: a distinctive personal portfolio with 3D and scroll-driven storytelling; plan concept, complete scroll, content, colour, type, mobile behaviour and other site needs. Explicitly no implementation.

Read both supplied files in material and the storyfolio skill's profile-reading reference.

Current stop: full storyboard awaiting review. Ines supplied corrections, audience, working documents and asset ownership/limits, and delegated remaining judgment. Answers are recorded under U1 in facts.md. Do not treat the delegation as permission to invent facts or use third-party work.

Completed: read asking, concept and storyboard references; documented three concepts; assistant selected The ferment log under delegated authority; wrote complete storyboard covering chapters/beats, colour/type, phone/accessibility fallbacks, site scope, performance targets and outstanding assets. Decisions recorded in decided-for-you.md.

Next: user approves storyboard or requests changes. Open publication dependencies are listed at the top of storyboard.md; optional third-party images do not block the plan. No implementation, installation or deployment performed. On storyboard approval, update this handover and explain that this skill version stops at planning.

item.text:
The direction is **The ferment log**: one continuous page answering **“What happens before the menu is written?”**

The complete plan is below and saved in [storyboard.md](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-with-Vei34y/docs/story/storyboard.md). Nothing has been built.

Items still needed before publication:

1. Your public contact details, workshop booking destination and apprentice enquiry route.
2. Your pot and larder photographs.
3. Restaurant permission for Priya’s photographs, with her credit, if included. Olu’s permission before using his drawings or scans containing them.
4. Confirmation of any current workshop dates or apprentice openings before advertising availability.

These do not prevent planning. The initial design works with sourced text and your own photographs.

**The idea and the object**

The site follows the order of your work: origins, dates, recording, checking, readiness, then what comes next. The menu appears after the preparation because that is how you say the kitchen operates.

One assembly of **six paper log leaves** carries the story. They open, spread into a timeline, align as working records, become a grid of evidence, compare measurements and gather again.

This is a designed interpretation of your ferment log. We have not seen the actual document, so the site will not pretend to reproduce its layout, handwriting or entries. Its fields come from you: date started, salt, check days and readiness.

The 3D has a specific job in each chapter: establish sequence, explain the record, reveal work or compare evidence. All important information also appears as readable page text.

**1. Started — the opening**

Approximately 1½ desktop screens.

The first screen contains:

- **Ines Okafor**, Head Chef at Saltmarsh, Leeds.
- Your focus on fermentation and apprentices.
- The central question.
- A compact proof point: the kitchen’s weekly waste falling from 14 kg to 5 kg, with team credit and its measurement context.
- An immediately visible enquiry link.

Beside this, the six leaves sit in a shallow, slightly open stack. Your photograph of your grandmother’s ogiri pot occupies the first visible face when supplied. A second face names the books you identified.

As the visitor scrolls, those leaves gently separate. The opening connects the object to your stated influences without inventing a childhood scene or a lesson you have not described.

**Visitors can:** jump to any chapter or go directly to enquiries. They do not need to wait for the opening animation.

**2. Date — where you have worked**

Approximately 1½ screens.

The leaves spread into an ordered chronology:

- Leeds Kitchen College, 2014–2016.
- Brassica, September 2016–May 2019.
- Fjaerland stage, January–March 2018, shown within that period.
- Corn Exchange Kitchen, June 2019–February 2022.
- Acting head chef at Saltmarsh, March 2022.
- Head Chef at Saltmarsh, September 2022 onward.

The Fjaerland leaf comes forward briefly. Its content specifies **a ten-week unpaid stage**, washing and labelling jars and helping with two batches of garum. It makes no research claim.

The chronology establishes experience without implying that the stage ended your Brassica employment or caused a later career decision.

**Visitors can:** expand concise role details using ordinary buttons or disclosure controls. Dates and role names stay visible without clicking.

**3. Salt — how the kitchen works**

Approximately 1½ screens.

Four leaves align into a working spread:

| Field | What the section explains |
|---|---|
| Date started | The record begins with when a jar was started. |
| Salt | Salt is recorded in the log. |
| Check days | The log records when it gets checked. |
| Ready | Readiness is recorded. |

The other leaves remain together at the edge, preserving the sense of one object.

The accompanying text explains the two documents you named: the prep list and ferment log. We show field names rather than inventing salt percentages, batch dates or instructions.

Near the end, another leaf becomes visible: the menu follows these records. This is the page’s central reveal—**the menu is written last each week**.

**Visitors can:** select a field to highlight its explanation. The explanations also remain available in ordinary text, so interaction is optional.

**4. Checks — the work itself**

Approximately 1½ screens.

The leaves arrange into a two-by-three grid. Their faces carry your own larder photograph and a cleared label detail, alongside sourced material about the koji cupboard, staff meal, workshops and Brine.

A readable work index accompanies the scene:

| Work | What appears |
|---|---|
| Larder and fermentation | Your photographs and the confirmed recording process. |
| Apprentice programme | Your role running it, with an enquiry route; no unconfirmed annual intake figure. |
| Workshops | Your first-Monday workshops, with confirmed practical details added before publication. |
| Brine | Your preserving zine, four issues from 2022–2025. Illustrations await Olu’s permission. |
| Sunday Pot | Your co-founder role and the supplied description of the Sunday meal using restaurant surplus. |

One leaf can move forward for closer inspection while the others remain in the grid.

Restaurant photographs can enrich this chapter after permission, with Priya’s credit. They are not necessary for the composition.

**Visitors can:** open available image details, close them with a button or Escape, and jump to apprentice or workshop enquiries. Images without a larger view will not look like buttons. Separate project pages are deferred.

**5. Ready — results and another person’s words**

Approximately 1½ screens.

Two leaves settle side by side:

**14 kg per week → 5 kg per week**

The qualification sits directly alongside the figures:

- A **whole-kitchen** result, credited as **“we.”**
- Prep and plate waste.
- Weighed over one month in 2023.
- Bones excluded because they go to stock.

The site will not extrapolate an annual saving or attribute the result to you alone or to a particular ferment.

A third leaf turns forward with Callum’s approved quotation:

> “Ines turned our bins into a larder. The best thing on the menu most weeks started as something we used to throw away.”

It is attributed to **Callum Reyes, owner of Saltmarsh**. The figures remain visible while the quotation appears.

**Visitors can:** read the full measurement context without opening a tooltip. This section needs no extra interaction.

**6. Next batch — the ending**

Approximately one screen.

The leaves gather into the original stack. The final face remains visible beside the contact section.

The story answers its opening question through what visitors have seen: preparation, recording and checking precede the weekly menu. Final wording will be written from those confirmed facts.

Three clear contact routes serve your audiences:

| Visitor | Action |
|---|---|
| Prospective apprentice | Enquire about the apprentice programme. |
| Workshop participant | View confirmed booking information or send a workshop enquiry. |
| Food writer | Contact you about your work. |

These can initially use one public email address with different subject lines. An existing booking service can receive workshop traffic once you provide its destination. We will not imply that applications are open or dates are available without confirmation.

The footer contains credits, privacy information as applicable and a return-to-top link.

**The look**

The selected palette is **Log paper**:

| Use | Colour |
|---|---|
| Background | Warm paper — `#F2EBDD` |
| Text | Dark ink — `#252A24` |
| Links and emphasis | Olive — `#46563D` |

The leaves have matte surfaces, faint ruling, subtle grain and soft edge shadows. Photographs provide the colour variation. Texture stays quiet enough to preserve readability.

Two typefaces:

- **Source Sans 3:** headings, paragraphs, navigation and buttons.
- **IBM Plex Mono:** dates, log fields and measured values.

Body text is approximately 18–20 px with comfortable line lengths. Headings have presence without overwhelming the photographs or records.

Two alternative palette studies remain documented: pale larder-label stock with green-blue accents, and cream paper with clay accents. The selected direction is Log paper; there is no need for a visitor-facing theme switcher.

**How scrolling and clicking feel**

On desktop, one scene stays alongside the text through the chapters. Scrolling changes its arrangement, with readable resting positions between movements.

The whole experience is approximately 8½ screens, adjusted to the actual content. Scrolling remains native: no forced slides, scroll interception or timed waits.

A slim navigation rail links to every chapter. Direct chapter URLs work. A contact shortcut stays easy to reach.

All actions have conventional buttons or links. Visitors never need to drag a 3D object to uncover essential information.

**On a phone, and without 3D**

| Situation | Experience |
|---|---|
| **Phone** | One column, with a compact chapter illustration above the text. The chronology becomes vertical, the evidence grid becomes stacked cards, and the two waste figures remain easy to compare. |
| **Small phone** | Static chapter illustrations by default. No prolonged pinned scene or sideways reading. |
| **Reduced motion** | Static arrangements replace scroll-linked movement. The chapter order and evidence stay intact. |
| **No WebGL / 3D unavailable** | Still images and ordinary paper-like panels replace the scene. All content and links work. |
| **No JavaScript** | A complete document with headings, photographs, native disclosure controls, chapter anchors and contact links. |

Touch targets are at least 44 px. No interaction depends on hovering. Keyboard focus is visible, images have useful descriptions, and the page supports zoom and reflow. Screen readers receive the complete text without duplicate narration from the decorative rendering.

**Everything else the site needs**

“Included” below means part of a future implementation; nothing is being built now.

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| Chapter navigation, skip link and contact shortcut | Included |
| Complete work index | Included, using confirmed descriptions |
| Individual project pages | Later, when sufficient material is available |
| Contact routes | Included; destinations needed |
| Workshop booking | Link to an existing service when supplied |
| New booking/payment system | Later, only if required |
| Downloadable CV | Outside this scope; you are not seeking employment |
| Callum’s testimonial | Included with attribution |
| Language | English initially |
| Search title and description | Included, with accurate identity and location |
| Shared-link preview | Included, using owned imagery or typography |
| Site icon | A simple folded log leaf |
| Missing-page screen | Included, linking back to the story and enquiries |
| Photo and illustration credits | Included |
| Blog | Deferred; Brine has a place in the work index |
| Chat | Outside this scope |
| Analytics | Omitted initially |
| Privacy/legal information | Matched to the actual operator, contact setup and services used |
| Domain, hosting and HTTPS | Needed for a future launch; no purchase or deployment now |
| Existing-site redirects | Decide once any existing site is identified |

For future maintenance, contact destinations, workshop information, image credits and work descriptions should be editable without changing the animation.

**Performance and verification**

Readable content loads before the scene. Images use appropriately sized files; 3D assets load afterward. The scene stops rendering when inactive.

Planning targets are under 500 KB for the initial mobile content, excluding deferred 3D, and approximately 1.5 MB for the desktop scene. These are budgets to verify during implementation.

Before launch, checks cover keyboard use, touch, narrow screens, reduced motion, disabled JavaScript and failed 3D rendering. Dates, measurement qualifications, credits and contact destinations receive a final content check. Supplier prices and unconsented faces must be removed from delivered assets themselves.

I have assumed enquiry-based contact, English, a standalone site and no invented batch records or unconfirmed numerical claims. Those decisions are recorded in [decided-for-you.md](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-with-Vei34y/docs/story/decided-for-you.md).

This completes the planning deliverable. The storyfolio workflow stops at planning, and your instruction remains explicit: **no building**.
